findings.reason: a node told "never collapsed ⇒ neither" can build that fixture with a legacy fingerprint, see a correct census "fail" its control, and repair the census into a wrong one.
findings.text: the second control says a review of a never-collapsed plan "must be counted as neither", but the pre-collapse form is the legacy *definition-ration* digest (plan_review.py:663-668, 280-290: section declarations are dropped from the current fingerprint precisely because a collapse rewrites them), so it differs from the current form for any plan carrying declarations, collapsed or not; a never-collapsed plan whose review was stored under the legacy definition matches the pre-collapse form only, and a correct census would count it pre-collapse-only, failing this control

findings.reason: the census is a standalone script that can enumerate live pointers itself and then call the reader per run, so the cited function still returns the same pointer data production reads.
findings.text: §2 has the census name "any live run whose write paths claim plan_review.py or _store.py, read from the crew claim reader declared_claim_paths", but `declared_claim_paths` (claims.py:85) takes one run id and its module docstring states nothing there "is wired to a command", so it cannot by itself enumerate live runs; the production claim enumeration is `list_live()` (routing.py:1043)

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `list_plan_reviews` (plan_review.py:1074), `delivered_reports`/`_delivered_report_sidecars` (1973/1925), `review_coverage` (781), `_fingerprint_forms` (678), `declared_claim_paths` (claims.py:85), `landed_section_ids` (_plan_html.py:557), `_apply_collapse_section` (_store.py:3191) and the `collapse_section` op (mcp.py:1269) all resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §2's second control asserts a never-collapsed plan "must be counted as neither", which encodes a false equivalence between collapse history and form match.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §2 writes to "the run's own report directory", a durable crew path, not a session scratchpad or node-local temp.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §2 introduces no code symbols; its prose names modules and functions by what they do and carries no plan labels, ticket numbers or version tags.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the census's live-run contention check names a reader that is wired to no command and takes a single run id, not a live-run enumeration.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 carries one deliverable (the read-only census and its report); the "names two things" sentence is part of that report, not a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — s3 declares `depends-on` on `the-fingerprint-has-one-form#s2` (meta `plan-section-depends-on`), s2 has no unmet dependency, and `plan-informs` names the plan that delegated this work; every relationship resolves to a node in this plan.
